claims.text: Sub-solidus annealing of equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi induces short-range chemical order.
Quenching preserves a near-random atomic configuration in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Short-range chemical order produces localized lattice distortions.
The localized lattice distortions created by short-range order act as heterogeneous obstacles to dislocation motion.
Under dynamic loading, these obstacles promote dislocation pinning.
Under dynamic loading, these obstacles increase dislocation interactions.
SRO-mediated resistance to dislocation motion raises the dynamic yield stress.
SRO-mediated resistance to dislocation motion enhances strain hardening.
The proposed SRO-mediated strengthening mechanism still permits ductile flow.
The near-random quenched state has lower dislocation resistance than the SRO-enhanced annealed state.
Annealed SRO-enhanced samples should exhibit higher dynamic yield stress than quenched samples.
Annealed SRO-enhanced samples should exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than quenched samples.
Annealing-induced SRO should modify the strain-rate-sensitivity curve relative to the quenched state, potentially shifting it to higher values.
The proposed behavior should hold from room temperature to approximately 0.4 Tm under dynamic loading.
The proposed behavior applies only when SRO is introduced without precipitation, significant grain growth, phase transformation, or other microstructural anomalies.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to samples in which annealing produces solely SRO, but the falsification rule says that finding additional annealing-induced modifications would especially support falsification. Such modifications instead place the experiment outside the stated boundary and confound attribution to SRO.
